newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan arrests 64 land tax protesters.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan arrests 64 land tax protesters.

text.p: Pakistan has arrested 64 farmers protesting against a new land tax and detained some of their leaders in the central province of Punjab, local officials said on Monday.
Under the tax farmers will have to pay a levy on every 12.5 acres (five hectares) of agricultural land. The existing tax is an annual 100 rupees per acre.

Saeed Ahmed, the top government official in Sargodha city in central Punjab, told Reuters that 64 members of Kissan Bacho Tehrik (Save the Farmers Movement) had been arrested in the past few days and five of their leaders were detained on Monday.
"Kissan Bacho Tehrik does not enjoy popular support, but it was creating a nuisance by blocking some roads in a few villages where they have concentration," he said.
Nasir Javaid Ghuman, the president of the movement, and four other people were detained when they staged a protest rally in Sargodha, Ahmed said.
Ghuman, fearing arrest, had been in hiding for the past few days and had only surfaced on Monday to address a public rally, his relatives said.
On Sunday the movement's officials said the government had arrested more than 300 farmers in the past two days in a bid to end the protest campaign.
A spokesman for the movement said it had blocked the supply of milk, vegetables and fodder into Sargodha city between July 25 to 27.
"This was a symbolic protest to press for our demands," Ghuman earlier told Reuters while hiding in Sargodha. "The agriculture income tax will hurt small farmers and we want its immediate repeal."
But Ahmed disputed the claim, saying there were "abundant supplies" of all commodities, including milk, vegetables and fodder during the protest.
He said there was minor trouble in only 10 out of more than 500 villages of Sargodha sub-district.
On Saturday, a collection of various farmers groups, Muthidda Kissan Mahaz (The Joint Farmers' Front), said it was prepared to discuss the agriculture tax with the government.

The front's acting chairman, Shah Mahmoud Qureshi, who is also a member of the opposition Pakistan People's Party, told Reuters that the farming community was angry over the imposition of the income tax, which he said had many flaws and had created unrest in villages.
He called on the government to impose the tax on every 50 acres of agricultural land.
